claims.statement: `ExecutorKind` (execution/types.ts:10) enumerates every runtime the server can name — 'mock', 'opencode', 'codex', 'claude', 'hermes', 'gemini', 'editor', 'pi', 'atomic', 'remote', 'docker', 'deep-agent', and 'custom'. The ExecutionEngine constructor always registers the ten defaults mock/opencode/codex/claude/hermes/gemini/editor/pi/atomic/remote and registers deep-agent only when `DJIMIT_DEEP_ENABLED=true` (also instantiating the DeepAgentContractIssuer).

`docker` and `custom` are the two ExecutorKinds never registered by the ExecutionEngine constructor: 'docker' only appears as the kind reported by DockerSandboxExecutor when the engine wraps another executor at dispatch time (created in startExecutionAttempt when sandbox.enabled is true), and 'custom' is the extension slot for out-of-tree implementations added via registerExecutor().

The TaskExecutor contract is `kind`, `start(task, options) → Promise<ExecutionSession>`, `canExecute(task) → boolean`, and optional `buildCommand(task, options) → { command, args }`; buildCommand is what lets DockerSandboxExecutor re-host an inner executor's CLI invocation without re-implementing argument construction.

`ExecutionSession` (types.ts:81-117) exposes `events: AsyncIterable<ExecutionEventCreateInput>` consumed by the engine's event pipeline, `result: Promise<ExecutionResult>`, `closed?: Promise<void>` (resolves only after the OS child and its stdio streams close), an `exit?: { code: number | null; signal: string | null }` recorded on the child's 'close' (absent when no child ran and preferred by LoopWorkerExecutorService.toRuntimeResult as the process exit), mandatory `cancel()`, and optional unimplemented `pause()`/`resume()`.

ExecutionFailure carries `retryable` and `sideEffectsPossible`; the engine's normalizeFailure forces retryable=false whenever sideEffectsPossible is true, and nextRetryExecutor refuses any retry if attempt >= maxRetries, !failure.retryable, or failure.sideEffectsPossible — so post-side-effect failures never chain-hop providers.

All spawn-path CLI adapters share runtime plumbing: runtime-process.ts (runtimeProcessClosed + SIGTERM→SIGKILL-after-5s stopRuntimeProcess that resolves on actual close), executor-env.ts `buildExecutorEnv` (an allowlist of PATH/locale/`*_API_KEY`/model/`*_BIN_PATH` vars plus `RUNTIME_ENV_PASSTHROUGH` extras, so server secrets stay out of spawned CLIs; a `SUBSCRIPTION_ENV_MARKER` on the env switches to subscriptionChildEnv, which drops every billing key and re-adds only the subscription login for the named runtime), `captureExecutorOutput` (rolling 5 MiB stdout/stderr tail), and structured-runtime-event.ts (maps tool_use/tool_result/error/text JSON chunks from claude/gemini/editor/codex/opencode/pi into TOOL_CALL/TOOL_RESULT/ERROR/LOG events with token usage).

The skip-permissions boundary is operator-armed: resolveExecutorSkipPermissions returns true only when task metadata requested it AND RUNTIME_ALLOW_SKIP_PERMISSIONS==='true', and ExecutionEngine.startExecutionAttempt only forwards skipPermissions to the adapter when that guard passes (a test asserts all four combinations). Per-executor * _SKIP_PERMISSIONS envs remain a second default layer.

DockerSandboxExecutor wraps an inner TaskExecutor, requires inner.buildCommand (else DOCKER_SANDBOX_INNER_COMMAND_UNAVAILABLE), reports kind:'docker', and enforces non-root user (1000:1000), --cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, read-only root + tmpfs /tmp (64 MiB), networkMode 'none' by default, cpu 1.0 / memory 512m, --rm cleanup, and a digest-pinned image (DOCKER_SANDBOX_IMAGE must contain @sha256:; DOCKER_SANDBOX_SKIP_DIGEST_CHECK=true bypasses with a warning and is NOT recommended for production). These invariants are asserted in docker-sandbox-executor.test.ts.

The engine creates a DockerSandboxExecutor inside startExecutionAttempt when task.metadata.sandbox.enabled===true, overriding image/cpu/memory/network/bind-mounts on DEFAULT_SANDBOX_CONFIG; deep-agent is explicitly forbidden from this Docker sandboxing path ('Deep Agent sandboxing is controlled by the sovereign runtime').

DeepAgentExecutor is gated on a signed contract: canExecute requires task.metadata.deep_agent_contract with identity.task_id matching this task and capabilities.profile_id==='no-tool-canary'; start() throws DEEP_AGENT_CONTRACT_INVALID_FOR_TASK otherwise. The remote transport accepts only an HTTP loopback or literal Tailscale IPv4 DJIMIT_DEEP_URL and fails closed on non-zero exit, timeout, oversized response, or unparseable final status.

deep-agent never participates in fallback: when its circuit breaker is open the engine throws instead of falling back, and nextRetryExecutor returns null for a failed deep-agent attempt — a contract-gated run is terminal by design.

CircuitBreakerService keeps per-ExecutorKind state CLOSED→OPEN→HALF_OPEN→CLOSED: CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD consecutive failures (default 3) in a 60s sliding window opens the circuit, canExecute returns false while OPEN until CIRCUIT_BREAKER_RECOVERY_MS (default 30s), then one probe is allowed in HALF_OPEN and 2 consecutive successes close it again.

FallbackChainService maps each ExecutionMode to an ordered provider list (fast: opencode→gemini→claude; standard: claude→codex→gemini; controlled: claude→codex; restricted: claude only) and getNextAvailable walks the chain after the current kind, skipping breakers that are open; custom chains can be injected via constructor or setChain().

maxRetries per attempt comes from ExecutionModePolicyService by mode (fast:1, standard:2, controlled:3, restricted:0), so even a retryable failure cannot chain-hop in restricted mode; fallbacks are re-admitted through the policy gate (fallbackAdmitted) and each hop is persisted with failureCode, failureDomain, retryable, and sideEffectsPossible.

The production Dockerfile pins `@openai/codex@0.146.0`, `opencode-ai@1.18.10`, and `@anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.282` globally and build-time-verifies all three binaries; it also installs the `gh` CLI as a static `.deb` pinned via `ARG GH_CLI_VERSION=2.102.1` (verified with `gh --version`) for GithubPrReviewService. At runtime `GET /swarms/runtime-readiness` treats only `codex` and `opencode` as production runtimes, checks contract availability/version and provider credentials, returns ready/blocked_reasons per runtime, and never starts a worker (`starts_workers: false`).

Before spawning a loop worker, LoopWorkerExecutorService (executeMaker L170-L197 and executeChecker L353-L375) probes the lease runtime via LoopService.getRuntimeContract(), records a `start` worker manifest with `gate_refs: ['runtime_contract']`, and when `!contract.available || contract.status !== 'ok'` records a `fail` manifest with `blocked_reasons: ['runtime_contract_drift']`, fails the lease with `failure_reason: runtime_contract_unavailable_or_drifted`, and throws RUNTIME_CONTRACT_DRIFTED — no provider process is spawned against a drifted contract.

RuntimeCommandService.getRuntimeContract probes each CLI runtime with <bin> --version plus a --help probe, marks the contract drifted when required json/cwd/headless flags are missing from the help output, stamps a sha256 conformance contract_hash with named checks (runtime_available, contract_not_drifted, structured_events, usage_accounting, bounded_lifecycle), caches contracts for LOOP_RUNTIME_CONTRACT_CACHE_MS (default 5s), and persists probes to the runtime_contract_probes table.

LoopService.getRuntimeContracts() (loop-service.ts:1395-1408) exposes manual, mock, codex, opencode, claude, gemini, editor, and pi at GET /loops/runtime-contracts (intentionally omitting atomic and remote); manual is always `ok` with proof_class static, but executeMaker rejects manual maker leases with MANUAL_MAKER_REQUIRES_HUMAN and manual checkers require an explicit non-manual runtime to dispatch (CHECKER_RUNTIME_REQUIRED).

OpenCodeExecutor has three run-safety behaviours: (1) a token brake — each `step_finish.part.tokens.total` feeds a running `tokenSum`, and when `OPENCODE_MAX_RUN_TOKENS` is set and the sum crosses it the executor stops the process mid-run and fails with a token-budget error; (2) step-progress events — `step_finish` reasons (`stop|length|content-filter|tool-calls|error|other`) map to a continuation/final/abnormal/error/unrecognized `step_outcome` and are always emitted as non-terminal events, so only the process exit decides the terminal completed/failed event; (3) verification-aware result — `tool_use` events for build_check/lint/test/typecheck or a bash command matching tsc|eslint|vitest|jest|pytest|cargo test|go test|npm test whose status or JSON output reports failure are recorded, and an exit-0 run with any such failure resolves `failed` with code VERIFICATION_FAILED (retryable: false, sideEffectsPossible: true).
CodexExecutor sums usage.input_tokens and usage.output_tokens from turn.completed NDJSON events into the result tokenUsage metric.

Before any task dispatch the ExecutionEngine runs `admitRuntime(taskId, executorKind)` (executeTask at L320 and again at every startExecutionAttempt at L626, so fallbacks are re-admitted), reading the runtime's observed version from Djimitflo's own `runtime_contract_probes` table and calling `checkAdmission()` on the in-repo `RUNTIME_ADMISSIONS` ledger. `checkAdmission` yields a deterministic verdict — REJECT on a critical-gate FAIL (licensing/reproducibility/supply_chain), self-attestation, or RUNTIME/SHARED authority ownership; HOLD or LEGACY_ADMITTED on unproven gates; only an in-date, version-matching executable record lets the run proceed and any other outcome is denied as RUNTIME_NOT_ADMITTED (recorded as a high-severity policy violation), with `RUNTIME_ADMISSION_MODE=shadow` as the record-but-don't-enforce rollback. The ledger lives in the repo so an assessment changes only through review, spanning the REJECT negative control (`openhuman`) through the LEGACY_ADMITTED incumbent (`opencode 1.18.10`).

AtomicExecutor (plan C5) is a gym-only maker species that spawns `atomic-agent run --cwd <dir> --max-steps N` with the goal written to stdin, and it stays inside Djimitflo's approval boundary by adding `--no-approval` only for a skip-permission-approved run; before each run it writes an OpenAI-compatible provider config (default Ollama Cloud, key from `OLLAMA_API_KEY` unless `ATOMIC_AGENT_API_KEY_ENV` names a var that may sit outside the allowlist) into a Djimitflo-owned `DJIMITFLO_ATOMIC_STATE_DIR`, so the operator's own ~/.atomic-agent is never touched.

RemoteMakerExecutor (plan I3) is the `remote` runtime — it spawns no local CLI; the lease's `model` names `<host>/<species>` (e.g. `workstation/atomic@llama-router`), the executor enqueues the job on RemoteMakerQueue only when the worktree's base commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, polls until the host returns a patch which is applied with `git apply --whitespace=nowarn`, and bounds work by REMOTE_MAKER_TIMEOUT_MS (default 30 min) plus an unclaimed-queue timeout REMOTE_MAKER_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_MS (default 45 min).

The production Dockerfile installs the Atomic Agent as a per-arch release tarball pinned by `ATOMIC_AGENT_VERSION=0.6.5` and per-arch `ATOMIC_AGENT_SHA256_X64`/`ATOMIC_AGENT_SHA256_ARM64` checksums (`sha256sum -c` during the build, linked to /usr/local/bin/atomic-agent, verified with `atomic-agent --version`), and it copies `packages/ransomware-module` source + package manifest in the builder stage so it is built and shipped in the production image; these pins exist so `runtime_contract` probes and the admission check see a deterministic `--version` output.

Loop worker dispatch (`executeViaEngine`, loop-worker-executor-service.ts:543-620) reuses an existing `execution_task_id` (surfacing LOOP_WORKER_EXECUTION_RECOVERY_REQUIRED on a server-restart hold, LOOP_WORKER_APPROVAL_REQUIRED, or LOOP_WORKER_EXECUTION_IN_PROGRESS) or otherwise inserts a real `tasks` row tagged `['loop-worker', role, runtime]` with the worktree prompt, nested-spawn env, optional `subscription_auth` marker env, and a get-or-create `<runtime>-<role>` agent identity before handing it to `ExecutionEngine.executeTask()`, so every loop worker flows through the same governance spine, circuit breaker, and runtime admission as a standalone task.
